profileEvidence.author: A
profileEvidence.summary: Close to its people yet strong-willed, the Miniature Dachshund combines an even manner with persistent hunting enthusiasm. These smaller Dachshunds were developed as compact burrow workers, without losing the wider breed’s skill at flushing and following wounded game. Intelligence and a keen nose run through all three coat varieties in this size class.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: An independent, people-oriented small hound, the Miniature Dachshund combines a keen nose with persistent hunting drive.

Full natural tail continues topline slightly downward; feet/limbs and proportions specified. Pages5–7 define red smooth coat and wild-boar wiry coat.

sources.title: Deutscher Teckelklub1888: Rund um den Hund
sources.evidence: Organized Zwerg/Kaninchen breeding began late19thcentury selecting small burrow dogs for young fox and especially rabbits; separate size books since1980s. Character paragraphs explicitly include smallest varieties: hunting passion, intelligence/teachability, seeking human proximity, retaining independence/strong will. Legacy current-size paragraph is superseded here by FCI2022 sex-specific ranges.
